spatial_claims.claim: D is a point taken within circle ABC
A, B, C are points on circle ABC
DA, DB, DC are straight lines from D to the circle with DA = DB = DC
Assume D is not the centre of circle ABC (for contradiction)
By Prop 3.7, since D is a non-centre interior point, only two equal straight lines can fall from D on the circle
Three equal straight lines DA, DB, DC fall from D on the circle, contradicting the maximum of two from 3.7

configuration_map: Circle ABC with interior point D. Points A, B, C lie on the circumference. Segments DA, DB, DC connect D to A, B, C respectively, all equal in length. D is interior to the circle throughout the proof. Any interior non-centre point lies on a diameter (the one through the centre and D), so Proposition 3.7 applies to D. The configuration is simple and static — no auxiliary constructions are made, no points change position, and the proof proceeds entirely by logical contradiction using a prior result.
pass_reason: The proof is a clean indirect argument with minimal spatial content. The only geometric claims are that D is inside the circle and that three equal lines run from D to the circumference. The application of Proposition 3.7 is valid because any interior non-centre point lies on a diameter, satisfying 3.7's hypothesis. No angle decompositions, betweenness claims, or interior/exterior arguments are made, so there is no opportunity for the characteristic configuration contradiction patterns. All spatial claims are mutually consistent.
